---
title: "Strand P · Pharmacology from the beginning"
subtitle: "Eighteen lessons that assume nothing"
---

Everything else on this site assumes you know what a receptor is. This strand
does not.

It exists because the field's newest and most useful people increasingly arrive
from statistics, mathematics, engineering and software — and there is no honest
on-ramp for them. The usual advice is "read a pharmacology textbook", which is
two thousand pages written for a different purpose. This is the subset a
quantitative scientist actually needs, in the order that makes the modelling
strands land.

**If you have a pharmacology, pharmacy or medical background**, skim `P-01` to
`P-05` for vocabulary and start at `P-06`. The ADME lessons are written to be
useful even when the biology is familiar, because they emphasise the quantities
rather than the mechanisms.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Nine of the eighteen carry runnable notebooks — wherever the pharmacology is
genuinely computational. The rest are prose, because forcing code onto the drug
development process or a tour of therapeutic areas would be contrived.
:::

## Part 1 · What a drug is, and what it acts on

| | Lesson | Runnable | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| P-01 | [What a drug is, and what it has to do](lessons/p-01-what-a-drug-is/) — the obstacle course from mouth to target; modalities and why they change everything | | **ready** |
| P-02 | [Cells, proteins, and why molecules stick together](lessons/p-02-cells-and-binding/) — the minimum molecular biology; what binding physically is | | **ready** |
| P-03 | [Drug targets](lessons/p-03-drug-targets/) — receptors, enzymes, transporters, ion channels; reading effect delay off the target family | | **ready** |
| P-04 | [Binding, quantified](lessons/p-04-binding-quantified/) — mass action, occupancy, residence time, what an IC₅₀ measures | ✓ | **ready** |
| P-05 | [Agonists, antagonists and everything between](lessons/p-05-agonists-and-antagonists/) — efficacy versus affinity, partial and inverse agonism, allosteric modulation, spare receptors | ✓ | **ready** |

## Part 2 · What the body does to the drug

| | Lesson | Runnable | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| P-06 | Absorption I: getting in — routes, gut physiology, dissolution, solubility and permeability, the BCS, food effects | | planned |
| P-07 | Absorption II: first pass and bioavailability — gut wall and hepatic extraction, efflux, why every oral parameter carries a `/F` | ✓ | planned |
| P-08 | Distribution — blood flow, plasma protein binding, tissue partitioning, barriers, what volume of distribution physically means | ✓ | planned |
| P-09 | Metabolism — phase I and II, the CYP families, induction and inhibition, prodrugs, reactive metabolites, pharmacogenomics | ✓ | planned |
| P-10 | Excretion — glomerular filtration, secretion, reabsorption, biliary elimination, enterohepatic recycling, renal impairment | ✓ | planned |

| | Lesson | Runnable | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| P-11 | The circulation and organ blood flows — cardiac output, perfusion, why flow limits clearance, and the reference numbers worth memorising | ✓ | planned |

| P-13 | Homeostasis, feedback and time — turnover of endogenous systems, circadian rhythm, tolerance, receptor regulation, disease progression | | planned |

## Free resources for this strand

Strand `P` is where a curriculum most often sends you to a textbook you have to
buy. These are the free alternatives, each checked (all on
[Resources](resources.qmd)):

**To learn from**

- [NIH *Principles of Clinical Pharmacology*](https://ocreco.od.nih.gov/courses/principles-clinical-pharmacology)
  — 48 recorded lectures on pharmacokinetics, drug metabolism and transport,
  special populations and pharmacogenomics. The closest free equivalent to the
  course this strand is trying to be.
- [MIT OpenCourseWare HST.151, *Principles of Pharmacology*](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/hst-151-principles-of-pharmacology-spring-2005/)
  — lecture notes, problem sets and exams **with solutions**, CC BY-NC-SA.

**To look things up in**

- [IUPHAR/BPS Guide to PHARMACOLOGY](https://www.guidetopharmacology.org/) —
  expert-curated targets with referenced affinity values across GPCRs, ion
  channels, nuclear receptors, kinases, transporters and enzymes. Where `P-03`
  and `P-04` send you for a real K~d~. CC BY-SA, so compatible with this site's
  own licence — one of the few sources here of which that is true.
- [FDA Table of Substrates, Inhibitors and Inducers](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-interactions-labeling/drug-development-and-drug-interactions-table-substrates-inhibitors-and-inducers)
  — which CYP and transporter probes are regulatorily acceptable, and for what.
  `P-09` and `P-10`.
- [DailyMed](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/) and
  [Drugs@FDA](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/daf/) — the current
  label, and the FDA clinical pharmacology review behind it. Reading one review
  for a drug you know teaches more about `P-17` than any summary can.
- [Reactome](https://reactome.org/) (CC0) and
  [WikiPathways](https://www.wikipathways.org/) (CC0) for pathway topology.
  Prefer these to KEGG, which despite appearances is **not** a public database
  and licenses commercial use separately.

**To get parameters from**

- [Open Systems Pharmacology PBPK model library](https://github.com/Open-Systems-Pharmacology/OSP-PBPK-Model-Library)
  — around 45 published, qualified whole-body PBPK models for real drugs,
  free to download and re-run. `P-11` and `P-12`.
- [EPA Physiological Information Database](https://cfpub.epa.gov/ncea/risk/recordisplay.cfm?deid=202847)
  — organ blood flows, tissue volumes and GFR across human life stages. A 2009
  static archive, and still the most complete free compilation of its kind.

## Where this sits

`P` comes before [`S0` Foundations](lessons/s0-00-what-is-qp/). Neither depends
on the other in a strict sense — you can read `S0-00` first for orientation, and
most people should — but every modelling strand from `S1` onward assumes the
pharmacology in `P`.

- **[Path C · The Crossover](paths/path-c-crossover.qmd)** starts here, and for
  many readers `P` plus `S0-06` is the whole destination.
- **[Path A · The New Modeler](paths/path-a-new-modeler.qmd)** and
  **[Path B · The Trainee](paths/path-b-trainee.qmd)** treat `P` as a named
  prerequisite: work it if the biology is not already yours, skip it if it is.
